subject: Google Protocol Buffer the whole MapReduce communication

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Google Protocol Buffer the whole MapReduce communication
parts:
Hi,

It occurred to me that if there is ever a rewrite of the internals of Rhipe that we should Google Protocol Buffer the whole communication between Java and C via pipes.


Right now the role of Google Protocol Buffers is to define the serialization of key value pairs via rexp.proto.  rexp.proto gets used in both the storage on the HDFS (map/sequence) and in the pipe data transfer from the Java MapReduce process to the RhipeMapReduce C program.

Inside of the communication between the Java and the C program is an ad hoc message format parsed in C here:
https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/blob/master/code/R/src/mapreduce.cc#L79

As you can the message format starts with a 64 bit integer.  That integer is either the number of bytes to read or if a negative integer it is a MapReduce "message" indicating the status of the Map or Reduce (ie  Map Setup, Mapping, Reduce Setup etc).  There is really no reason to be doing that work "by-hand" if we are already depending on protobuf.  One can imagine writing another mapreduce.proto that defines the messages and  buffers of rexp.proto as necessary.


This would have the advantage of clear documentation of Java and C communication , automatic generation of parsing classes from C and Java, and  perhaps make easier future changes to the communication between Java and C, while also making one of the messiest pieces of code easier to read.  I wonder if it would even do away with all the big-indian little-indian parsing issues that are buried in the C code (perhaps indicating that the result is more portable too since we have offloaded the C and Java communication to Google classes?)



It isn't actually a hard change.  It is just a change that touches on everything Rhipe does so it is high risk.

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Google Protocol Buffer the whole MapReduce communication
parts:
To be clear there are currently two types of communication between processes in Rhipe:
Pass by environmental variable
Pass by buffer

I was just thinking about the pass by buffer situation as it is the easiest target for Google Protocol Buffer replacement. In retrospect the environmental variables could be done away with too (more later).

I cooked up a prototype .proto file here: https://gist.github.com/jrounds/5522736  This file passes a build through "protoc" but hasn't been dropped into code yet.

It is meant to be a drop in replacement of Rhipes ad hoc pipe communication rather then a re-imagining of Rhipe's engineering.

The key messages are "FromHadoopMapReduce" and "ToHadoopMapReduce".

The FromHadoopMapReduce contains a state (required) which you designed and then "optional" and "repeated" RExp or Rexp Key, value pairs depending on state. So here already is one thing made easier: We have off loaded the reading of entire buffers of repeated values to Google.

So the pseudo-code is something like
MapReduce Engine in C:
  read first FromHadoopMapReduce message using bool ParseFromIstream(istream* input);
  dispatch to function corresponding to message.state  
  evaluate whether ToHadoopMapReduce message needs to be pushed to Java yet via SerializeToOstream(&output)

The dispatch functions would be like:
int map_setup(FromHadoopMapReduce message);
int map_map(FromHadoopMapReduce message);
int map_cleanup(FromHadoopMapReduce message);
int reduce_pre(FromHadoopMapReduce message);

etc.

I would just use global variables between dispatches of MapReduce engine to keep it simple.  For example, https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/blob/master/code/R/src/mapreduce.cc#L205 mainMapperLoop has several buffer variables it needs.   Just g_ them and make them global.  You don't want static because you want map_setup to be able to initialize them.

example pseudo-code for one particular function:

map_map (FromHadoopMapReduce* message):
   Rexp KV to Sexp KV (message->map_data, g_sexp_buffers)
   do Rf_setvars from g_sexp_buffers
   do Rf_eval of map expression
   push to combiner buffer if combining push to global gp_ToHadoopMapReduce->data if not
   check to see if combiner needs to execute
   return



The design of FromHadoopMapReduce is so close to your design that the code would write easily.  I am willing to do it, I just need to know someone else cares, and someone else will help me validate that it is correct.

Thanks

messages.author: a5ca085497920157
messages.subject: Re: Google Protocol Buffer the whole MapReduce communication
parts:
I was messing with code and I realized it doesn't make a lot of sense to hold many key, value pairs in one message.  They should still come one at a time so that you arn't wasting more memory then you need too.  The basic idea of letting google protocol buffer do the parsing to and from Java is valid though.

The code is rough drafting like what follows.  In design it is very similar to what you originally had in Rhipe's C code about a year ago before I rewrote it, but it will be easier to modify this way.



struct s_map_data {
FromHadoopMapReduce pb_in;
ToHadoopMapReduce pb_out;
        // Everything mappers use will get dumped in here too.

} g_map_data;
/*
 * execMapperWithCombiner
 * The WithCombiner is to remind us that we sometimes combine.
 * Most of the combining logic is actually in collect_buffer.
 * We only have setup and cleanup here.
 * input: fin what file to take Map Key,Value pairs from.  Currently not used.
 */
int map_setup() {
int ret;
setupCombiner();
if ((ret = mapper_setup()) != 0) {
LOGG(12,"FAILURE IN MAP SETUP:%d ",ret);
merror("Error while running mapper setup: %d ", ret);
return 0;
}
return 1;

}
//if force == true then use map expression when buffer is not full.
//if force == false then may not do anything if buffers arn't full.
int execMapExpression(bool force);
int runCombiner(bool force);
int map_map(){
//place contents of g_map_data.pb_in.map_data into buffer
execMapExpression(false);
runCombiner(false);
return 1;
}
int map_cleanup(){
execMapExpression(true);
runCombiner(true);
SEXP cleaner;
int Rerr;

//do we really need to evaluate type to see if we should be doing this?  Don't see why...
Rf_defineVar(Rf_install(".rhipe.current.state"),Rf_ScalarString(Rf_mkChar("map.cleanup")),R_GlobalEnv);
PROTECT(cleaner=rexpress(MAPCLEANS));
R_tryEval(Rf_lang2(Rf_install("eval"),cleaner),NULL,&Rerr);
UNPROTECT(1);
return 1;
}

void execMapperWithCombiner(FILE* fin){
bool finished = false;
while(!finished){
g_map_data.pb_in.ParseFromIstream(&cin);
int state = g_map_data.pb_in.state();
switch(state){
case MapReduceState::MAP_SETUP:
map_setup();
break;
case MapReduceState::MAP_MAP:
map_map();
break;
case MapReduceState::MAP_CLEANUP:
map_cleanup();
finished = true;
break;
default:
LOGG(12,"Error Unexpected state in execMapperWithCombiner:%d ",state);
   merror("Error unexpected state in execMapperWithCombiner: %d ", state);
   break;
}


cout << g_map_data.pb_out;
g_map_data.pb_out.Clear();

}


}

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Google Protocol Buffer the whole MapReduce communication
parts:
It will take some time.  

For the Java side I believe everything runs through RHBytesWriteable.

https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/blob/master/code/java/org/godhuli/rhipe/RHBytesWritable.java

What makes this feasible is that RHBytesWritable has numerous child classes that all kindly create a RExp object but then turn it into bytes.  For example, https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/blob/master/code/java/org/godhuli/rhipe/RHText.java. Then RHBytesWritable::write takes those bytes and writes out their length and then them. https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/blob/master/code/java/org/godhuli/rhipe/RHBytesWritable.java#L113

There is a two step "recipe" to getting this into the Java side for each of the child classes:
1) For each RHBytesWritable sub class put the Rexp into a MapReduce Message proto object with a state or message integer field. 
2) Stop RHBytesWritable from writing out the bytes in front of proto object and just let the proto object serialize out to the pipe.


That is the strategy, but as I write it out I am 100% positive there are nagging little details that will be troubling.

For example, the writable to C from Java needs to be split from the writable from Java to Hadoop classes.  RHbytesWritable does double duty in that regard I think.  I think the cleanest rewrite will have one quickly converted into the other perhaps via a field.


I will get back to you if anything comes from this.
